title: The Joyita
subtitle: South Pacific · 1955
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the open South Pacific Ocean in the mid-1950s, a small white wooden motor vessel, deep blue water and pale tropical sky, faded Kodachrome colour, melancholy and uncanny, vertical 9:16 full-bleed composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: South Pacific, November nineteen fifty-five. A small ship was found drifting north of Fiji. Everyone aboard was gone.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: a small 1940s wooden motor vessel, about seventy feet long, white hull and low deckhouse, centred in frame and well lit by clear tropical daylight, listing heavily to one side on a calm deep-blue Pacific, empty decks, no one aboard, the whole boat clearly legible against bright water.

beats.vo: The Joyita had left Samoa five weeks earlier, on a two-day run to Tokelau, with twenty-five people aboard.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: an empty wooden harbour jetty in Apia at dawn in the 1950s, coconut palms and a calm lagoon, pale gold light, mooring ropes coiled on the planks where a boat had been, no people.

beats.vo: She was found more than six hundred miles off course, partly submerged, kept afloat by the cork lining her hull.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: low angle along the waterline of a small white wooden motor vessel, her port rail awash, sea water lapping over the deck, broken deckhouse windows, endless empty blue ocean beyond, hard midday light, no people.

beats.vo: Her radio was tuned to the distress frequency. The clocks had stopped at ten twenty-five. The life rafts were gone.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: inside a cramped 1950s wheelhouse, an old valve radio set with a glowing dial beside a small round wall clock with stopped hands, salt-stained wood panelling, daylight through a cracked window, no people, no legible text.

beats.vo: No one aboard was ever found. The inquiry called their fate inexplicable on the evidence.
beats.img: Vertical full-bleed scene: a vast empty South Pacific at dusk seen from high above, one tiny white boat alone on the darkening water far below, a long pale wake fading, soft violet and amber sky, unresolved and silent.

facts.claim: MV Joyita found 10 November 1955 drifting north of Fiji (north of Vanua Levu) by the merchant ship Tuvalu, no one aboard
Left Apia, Samoa on 3 October 1955 bound for the Tokelau Islands, scheduled arrival 5 October (a two-day run), 25 aboard: 16 crew, 9 passengers
Found more than 600 miles (about 970 km) off her route, partly submerged and listing heavily, kept afloat by cork lining in the hull
Radio tuned to 2182 kHz, the international marine distress channel; clocks stopped at 10:25; the three Carley liferafts and the dinghy missing
No one aboard was ever found; the February 1956 inquiry in Apia found their fate 'inexplicable on the evidence submitted at the inquiry'; no new findings reported as of May 2025
